title: Fragmentation-aware memory planner for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen with continuous batching
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Problem: Long-context workloads (32k-64k+ tokens) dramatically increase KV cache footprint and expose GPU allocator fragmentation under continuous batching. Different model families and quantization formats (Llama q4/q5, Mistral q8, Qwen variants) have different per-layer buffer sizes and transient allocations which lead to inconsistent worst-case resident memory and occasional OOMs under peak load.

Goal: Implement a fragmentation-aware memory planner that produces per-model, per-quantization allocation templates and runtime heuristics for: (1) tiled KV allocations to reduce internal fragmentation, (2) proactive KV eviction/pruning thresholds based on prefix-reuse heuristics, (3) allocator free-list tuning and opportunistic compaction for long-running workers, and (4) continuous-batching aware memory reservations so batch join/split phases do not trigger OOMs. The planner should be pluggable into the serving runtime and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: Llama 2 family (7B/13B/70B variants), Mistral large variants, and Qwen-14/Chat variants. Focus on long-context configs (32k, 64k) and common quant packs (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0). Deliverables: per-variant allocation templates, runtime switches for eviction aggressiveness, tests/benchmarks, and a rollout plan with canary configs in internal Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Peak resident GPU memory reduced by >=12% on targeted long-context traces for at least two model families compared to current baseline
<2% OOM incidence on 10k synthetic steady-state continuous-batching sessions for each model/quantization pair
P99 token latency within 10% of baseline for the same throughput (no regressions that break latency SLO)
Per-model allocation templates validated and checked into runtime config with documentation for ops/SEs
Automated benchmarks (CI) that exercise long-context tiling and KV eviction heuristics included in runtime-1.22 release pipeline
updates: 2026-02-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope and metrics. Agreed to prioritize Llama-13B q4 and Mistral-7B q8 as first variants for prototyping.

2026-02-10: Profiling pass across internal traces (synthetic and customer-replay). Found two main fragmentation hotspots: (A) transient CUDA mallocs during batch concat phases, (B) KV slab sub-allocations from variable-length attention heads.

2026-02-18: Prototype allocator changes merged to local branch: slab-tiling for KV blobs + adjustable free-list bucket sizes. Brief perf: peak mem -9% on Llama-13B 64k trace, p99 latency +4% during join operations. Details: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2345

2026-02-25: Experimented with prefix-based KV pruning policy (age+reuse score). Early results: reduced steady-state KV size by ~15% on traces with high prefix reuse; introduced slight increase in token recomputations for low-reuse traces. Added metric: "kv_recompute_rate" to console dashboards.

2026-03-03: Added continuous-batching reservation: reserve a small tail buffer per worker to cover worst-case join op allocations. This removed 92% of join-time OOMs in stress tests but increased baseline resident memory by ~3%. Decision: make reservation configurable per deployment tier (hosted: aggressive, dedicated: conservative).

2026-03-10: Integration test in internal Dedicated cluster: Llama-13B q4_0, 64k context, steady ingestion at 400 rps with variable batch sizes. Observed peak memory down 18% vs baseline, OOMs zero across 6h run. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2389

2026-03-12: Preparing rollout plan — canary 5 nodes in dedicated-us-east-1 for runtime-1.22. Noted outstanding tasks: final telemetry dashboards for fragmentation metrics, docs for SE runbooks, and QA signoff on Mistral/Qwen templates.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive compaction reduces peak footprint but may increase CPU/GPU sync and slightly increase p99; opted for opportunistic compaction during low-latency windows.
Quantization differences: q4 allocations have tighter per-block packing but are more sensitive to head-size variance; templates must encode per-layer alignment constraints.
Operational runbook: include quick toggle to revert tiling and to increase reservation size in case of regressions; SEs to monitor 'kv_recompute_rate' and 'allocator_frag_ratio' metrics.
Next steps: tune eviction thresholds per-customer workload, add CI fuzzing for random long-context sequences, and finalize canary checklist.
